claims.exact_statement: For finite controlled HMMs with symbol matrices M_m^(u,o), equality of pi_m M_m^(u1,o1)...M_m^(uL,oL)1 for every finite action/output word is equivalent to equality of transcript laws under every finite adaptive policy. If the models are distinguishable, a witness word exists with length at most n1+n2-1.
assumptions: finite hidden-state counts n1,n2 are supplied
a fixed discrete sampling interface with matrices M_m^(u,o)
policy randomization is independent of the mechanism
claims.novelty_boundary: Controlled-word formulation and dimension bound are standard finite-state HMM/weighted-automaton reasoning; no new general HMM theorem claimed.
claims.costs: Enumeration of schedules through length n1+n2-1 can be exponential in the hidden-state bound and action/output alphabet; finite-data guarantees additionally require a positive uniform TV margin and charge rate acquisition, assay precision, and independent units.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the finite-word matrix representation or span-stabilization proof under the stated interface would refute the lemma; continuous-time observations outside the fixed finite representation are outside scope.
claims.next_gate: Compare a certified finite-word search and robust schedule mixture against controlled-HMM and active Markov-chain experiment-design implementations at equal observation and action cost.

claims.exact_statement: There is a finite 10-state hidden CTMC whose actionwise observable chemical-Langevin drift and covariance agree pointwise at every observable x, hidden h, and action for all values of an unknown active hidden-switch rate theta, while passive x-path laws are identical for all theta and a fixed active pulse separates theta values through a second-order survival-probability contrast.
assumptions: observable state x is in {0,1,2,3,4}; latent phase h is in {0,1}
at x=2, h=0 jumps +/-1 at rate c each and h=1 jumps +/-2 at rate c/4 each
at x!=2, the common reset action jumps x to 2 at rate kappa; other actions leave x fixed
hidden h flips at rate zero under passive/reset and unknown theta under active
CLE b,A are computed only for the observable x increments; hidden flips have x increment zero
claims.status: internally_proved_exact_generator-and-moment construction; finite arithmetic check; no biological extrapolation
claims.novelty_boundary: Finite-state construction using standard moment matching and killed-CTMC formulas; no novelty or priority claim.
claims.costs: Requires single-cell jump-size/time observations, independent biological units, passive phase readout from jump marks, reset action, and explicit rate bounds or confidence sets; natural-system acquisition cost is unknown.
claims.falsifier: Within the model, algebraic equality b=0,A=2c at the center and the derived survival contrast are exact. A biological realization is falsified if measured rates, jump marks, hidden switching, or survival contrasts violate the specified generator.
claims.next_gate: Find a named biological state/readout interface where first-two-moment fields can be estimated and the required jump marks and active pulse are measurable.

claims.exact_statement: For the point candidate rates theta=0.1 versus theta=3, nuisance c in [0.9,1.1], and an active pulse of duration 1, the survival endpoint ranges are disjoint for either known starting hidden phase. After a passive mark/reset pilot identifies the phase, at most 7,207 independent active pulses suffice for 5% per-hypothesis testing error even when phase mixture is unknown, using a phase-centered score and Hoeffding.
assumptions: the event-rate multiplier c is fixed per model in the supplied interval [0.9,1.1]
each replicate's initial h is revealed by a passive jump mark, h remains frozen during passive/reset, and reset returns x to 2
independent replicate outcomes across biological units
active test records whether x remains 2 at time 1
claims.status: conditional finite-sample bound; formulas checked numerically in double precision; cell rates and assay assumptions are illustrative
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard exponential-matrix calculation and Hoeffding bound; not a real-world power calculation.
claims.costs: Per unit charge passive phase-mark waiting (expected at most 2/0.9), reset waiting (at most 1/kappa_min), one unit active pulse, endpoint read, and culture/assay costs. This is 7,207 independent units in the robust mixture-free example.
claims.falsifier: Finite example arithmetic fails if computed survival ranges overlap or sample-bound arithmetic is wrong; biological application is falsified by model misspecification or dependent/nonrepresentative units.
claims.next_gate: Use pilot confidence sets for c,kappa and certify the margin over full theta intervals; return UNKNOWN if the margin is not positive.

claims.exact_statement: For compact unknown-rate classes with supplied finite hidden-state bounds and no cross-class IO-equivalent pair, finite word enumeration through length n1+n2-1 gives a positive robust separation margin; a maximin action-schedule mixture followed by nearest-set classification has a finite categorical sample bound. If the robust margin is zero, no uniform finite-data identification guarantee follows.
assumptions: compact parameter confidence sets and continuous finite-word output laws
finite observation alphabet and fixed horizon/sampling grid
cross-class IO equivalence is absent for a positive uniform result
independent replicate trajectories for the stated empirical-law bound
claims.status: internally derived conditional compactness/design argument; robust continuous optimization is not implemented or certified
claims.novelty_boundary: Robust experiment design and confidence-set reach-avoid optimization are standard in substance; application-specific certificate and biological relevance remain open.
claims.costs: Action schedules scale exponentially with horizon/state bound; rate-set global optimization, matrix exponential precision, sample alphabet size, interventions, readouts, and safety screening must be charged.
claims.falsifier: A compact pairwise distinguishable family with zero minimum finite-word TV margin would refute the compactness argument; noncompact rate sets or unbounded hidden-state order are outside assumptions.
claims.next_gate: Implement interval-certified policy and parameter search on a real finite-rate confidence set and compare against adaptive controlled-HMM baselines.
